a calibrative modeling approach based on a small number of physicochemical descriptors can be employed to estimate the solubility over an entire pH range of a series of protein mutants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational approach to protein solute modeling.
the development and evaluation of a calibrative modeling approach that employs physicochemical properties routinely measured in bio-analytical labs for predicting protein solubility.

developing a predictive approach to protein solute behavior in solution based on physicochemical parameters that can be measured experimentally or estimated in silico from the protein’s crystal structure.

the physicochemical properties employed in the calibrative models can be estimated in silico and that these models are useful in predicting solubility trends in the absence of a detailed understanding of the protein’s structure.

a simple calibrative model can be used to predict the solubility behavior of a mutant series with a limited amount of experimental information.
